There’s just certain jobs computers & AI can’t do. That’s why we’re reinvesting in the heart and soul of our nation: the American worker.

Indiana steel continues to build our future. Under President Biden, we’ll keep supporting our workforce with good policies & more resources. https://t.co/6eXbqw1YWt

Today’s @HouseIntel committee hearing makes it clear: the more we strengthen and diversify our workforce—across sectors, but especially the intelligence community—the better our capability to tackle world threats, including AI, Biotechnology, and cybersecurity. https://t.co/cpLwH3Smfl

Today, I helped lead a @CmteOnCCPDems hearing with AI leaders about what American companies are doing to stay competitive in the global race toward Artificial Super Intelligence. Generative AI models are rapidly evolving, and the U.S must continue to lead the industry while also ensuring American privacy, jobs, and our national security remain intact.

If Chinese AI models win, we face a future filled with censorship and surveillance. Not to mention, in the key industries of the future – including sectors like manufacturing and biotechnology that drive Indiana's economy – we will fall behind.

But if American AI models keeps its lead, the American people will get to decide on the rules of the road. We can enact protections for workers against displacement, ensure communities do not face hikes to their utility bills, and ensure civil rights and human rights are designed into the algorithms.

Meanwhile, the Defense Department is trying to put one of our leading AI labs out of business because of a contract dispute. Killing Claude doesn't help us beat China. That sounds to me like benching one of our top scorers in a championship game.
The future of AI must be built on American values – and not the CCP's dystopian vision of censorship and surveillance. I believe we can keep our edge and win the future if we get to work.

The stakes of AI – especially with China – could not be higher. 
 
If Chinese AI models win, we face a future of censorship and surveillance, and fall behind on sectors like manufacturing that drive Indiana’s economy. 
 
I led a hearing on why American AI must lead – to protect consumers and prepare for the future.

BILL  ALERT: I’m co-leading the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act.  Data centers are often shrouded in mystery, with plans moving forward before meaningful public input. My bill will require data centers to be transparent. Neighborhoods have to deal with the consequences of data centers – and so neighborhood input should be central, not an afterthought.

When Americans answer the call to serve, we have a responsibility to support them when they return home. That’s why I introduced amendments to strengthen VA medical research, protect food security programs for veterans, and require bias reviews for AI systems used by the VA and Department of Defense.

Data centers cannot come at a cost to American families, who are already facing high grocery, gas, and housing costs. Data centers have the potential to create good union jobs, but they also have the potential to eliminate jobs. We need to make sure workers, families, and neighborhoods aren't forced to pay the burden of this rapidly rising technology without guardrails.

I'm supporting a nationwide pause on all new AI data centers until safeguards are put in place — protecting union jobs and your energy bill. 

I also introduced my Data Center Transparency Act to make sure neighborhood feedback is central. 

In Irvington, residents continue to make their voices heard, including at today’s hearing. 

You deserve transparency. You deserve affordability. You deserve a seat at the table.

Yesterday, the House passed my @ACLU -endorsed amendment requiring public reports on how the military uses AI. 
 
Weapons of war shouldn’t be handed to algorithms without human judgment and strong safeguards.

As AI plays a growing role in our national defense, Americans deserve transparency and accountability. This past week, the House passed my amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act requiring public reports on how the military is using AI and what safeguards are in place.

The Republican majority must bring Democrats' AI Civil Rights Act to the House floor. It's abundantly clear we need to better regulate AI to protect Americans, not to make tech billionaires even richer.

Speaker Johnson sent Congress home early instead of holding a vote on common sense AI regulations — giving a free pass to tech billionaires. I joined 106 of my colleagues to demand Congress take action. The risks are clear and urgent, and we need to act now.
https://t.co/6n43D06pMT

Republican leadership canceled votes Thursday instead of taking action on AI. There is ample evidence of cybersecurity concerns, surveillance, and the risk of rogue AI agents. Instead of addressing these concerns, Speaker Johnson is giving a free pass to tech companies. The pace of AI development means these are urgent concerns. AI needs to be regulated – and we need to act now.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is already changing how we live. It is a powerful tool that can do a great deal of good, but without clear safeguards, it can also harm– especially as it grows faster than we can keep up with.

AI can have staggering impacts on public health, the economy, and our communities. It is also increasingly being used in our military. When the stakes are high, we need to make sure a human is making decisions, not a machine.
